findings.title: Adversarial evidence corpus retains 4/26 documented Escape outcomes
findings.evidence: crates/fornax-bench/src/adversarial.rs::corpus() tallied live against candidate SHA 742c6d7: 11 Detected, 10 Prevented, 4 Escaped, 1 Inconclusive. The 4 Escaped fixtures (forged trust-class label authenticity; cross-claim evidence replay; FORNX-347's SourceFamilyMap O(n^2 log n) scalability gap) are individually documented in the corpus module's own doc comments and were disclosed, not hidden, by FORNX-380/381/385's own PRs. Full evaluation recorded in FORNX-392's gate comment.

findings.title: No daemon/acquisition-identity binding concept yet (FORNX-381 AC2)
findings.evidence: crates/fornax-types/src/provenance_guard.rs hardens sensor/trust-class authorization and payload-metadata spoofing, but cross-session attribution at the daemon/acquisition-identity layer is not yet a modeled concept in this codebase -- disclosed in FORNX-381's own PR body and re-confirmed by this session's independent code review; FORNX-381 remains DEV VERIFY, not Done, for exactly this reason.

findings.title: FORNX-383's second Kani proof target (acquisition-authorization state machine) is formally unverified
findings.evidence: cargo kani proof harnesses for the acquisition-authorization state machine compile but hit a real CBMC out-of-memory (~9GB, confirmed via ps during FORNX-383's own investigation) caused by Vec::sort()'s generic internals -- a tooling resource limit, not a discovered design flaw. The first target (key_temporal_status freshness logic) has 4 genuinely verified Kani proofs, independently re-run by this session against the merged main commit.
